headline: Bitcoin is back above $61,000 on Monday evening in Bangkok as US stock futures rebound, but money is still leaving bitcoin funds ahead of a short US holiday week with inflation data on Wednesday.

market.asOf: Read from the CoinMarketCap homepage at about 11:59 UTC Mon 23 Nov (18:59 Bangkok); the direction of the 24h moves could not be read, so it is left blank. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 11 out of 100 ("Extreme Fear") on the alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index; CoinMarketCap's own index showed 9 ("Extreme fear"). Both read at about 11:59 UTC Mon 23 Nov.

stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back above $61,000 as Wall Street futures rebound
stories.summary: Bitcoin recovered from its weekend low of about $55,100 and was back above $61,000 on Monday as US stock futures jumped about 3% after the Nasdaq's worst week since March 2020. Bitcoin also ended a record 18-day run of lower daily highs, which CoinDesk calls only an early signal. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index is still at "Extreme Fear".
points: Bitcoin was about $61,350 on Monday morning US time, per CoinDesk; its weekend low was $55,106, about 37% below its September peak, per CoinDesk.
S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 3% before the US open, after the Nasdaq fell 10.4% last week, per CoinDesk.
South Korea's KOSPI closed down 3.31% at 4,708.54 on Monday, per Seoul Economic Daily.
CoinDesk says a lasting recovery would need money flowing back into bitcoin funds and stablecoins.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving bitcoin funds before a short Thanksgiving week with inflation data
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin funds lost money for another week, and traders still expect the Fed to raise rates in December. October PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, comes out on Wednesday, and US stock markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving while crypto keeps trading.
points: Sources disagree on last week's bitcoin fund outflows: $1.79 billion, the fourth losing week in a row, per The Block citing SoSoValue; $1.24 billion, per FxPro citing SoSoValue in CoinDesk's live blog.
BlackRock's IBIT lost $1.37 billion and US spot ether funds lost $314 million, their eighth losing week in a row, per The Block.
Total assets in US spot bitcoin funds were $71.35 billion on Friday, down from about $110 billion in mid-September, per The Block.
CME FedWatch odds of a quarter-point December hike: more than 95%, per CoinDesk; 93.2%, per KuCoin. Bets on a half-point hike have fallen to zero, per CoinDesk.
US stock markets and the spot crypto funds are closed Thursday 26 Nov and close early on Friday 27 Nov; crypto itself trades through the holiday, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Kalshi faces a New York court hearing today that it says could shut it down
stories.summary: New York's Attorney General is asking a state court for a renewed restraining order against the prediction market Kalshi. Kalshi says the order's wording would effectively shut down the whole exchange; the Attorney General's office says it is not seeking a nationwide shutdown.
points: Justice Melissa Crane hears the request at 11:30am ET Mon 23 Nov (23:30 Bangkok) in New York County Supreme Court, per Inside Bitcoins.
The order would bar unlicensed gambling contracts "within or from New York or to persons in New York", covering sports, elections and other events, per Inside Bitcoins.
On Fri 20 Nov a federal judge rejected the CFTC's second emergency bid to block New York's case, per Inside Bitcoins.

briefs.title: Chainflip hack bounty deadline is today
briefs.summary: Chainflip's 10% bounty offer ends at 18:38 UTC Mon 23 Nov (01:38 Tue Bangkok); losses total about $12 million, including 122.86 BTC, and the stolen ETH and stablecoins went through Tornado Cash, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin briefly sold for about $17,000 on Kraken's Canadian-dollar market
briefs.summary: Bitcoin traded at C$24,250 on Kraken's Canadian-dollar market early Saturday, far below global prices; Kraken says the trades stand and it found no breach, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Monad's large MON unlock is Tuesday
briefs.summary: CoinDesk puts Tuesday's MON unlock at about $217 million, about 140% of circulating supply. See the unlock table on this page for this desk's size and confidence.

briefs.title: South Korea to publish a draft Digital Asset Basic Act
briefs.summary: The draft, due this week, proposes a 15-20% cap on major shareholders' stakes in exchanges and bank-majority issuers for won stablecoins, per The Block.

briefs.title: Japan steps up crypto tax audits
briefs.summary: Tokyo's tax bureau found about 3.9 billion yen (about $24.5 million) of hidden crypto trading income among 91 audited users, per CoinDesk citing NHK.

briefs.title: Visa tests an AI agent wallet paid in a stablecoin
briefs.summary: Visa Crypto Labs launched an experimental wallet for eligible US cardholders whose AI agents earn 10-50 OUSD for paid tasks such as surveys, per The Block.

briefs.title: Swedish bitcoin treasury firm lost 30 BTC trading
briefs.summary: H100 Group lost about 30 BTC (about $1.8 million) trading part of its holdings in the third quarter; its long-term treasury holds 3,243 BTC, per CoinDesk.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (September 3.1%) and headline at 3.8% (September 3.6%), per Asktraders; RBC expects core at 3.3%, per CoinCentral. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% per Thrive in Markets or 3.4% per Asktraders. Jobless claims are expected at 201K per Thrive in Markets (prior 203K).
The last Fed publication before officials go quiet on policy, per Thrive in Markets. New home sales come out at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok); 650K is expected after 676K, per Asktraders.
NYSE is closed Thursday and closes early at 1:00pm ET on Friday 27 Nov (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per NYSE's holiday calendar. Crypto trades through the holiday.

Per the BLS release schedule; it comes out before the Fed's 8-9 Dec meeting.

calendar.note: Per the Federal Reserve's calendar; officials' quiet period starts Sat 28 Nov. Odds of a quarter-point hike: more than 95% per CoinDesk, 93.2% per KuCoin (both citing CME FedWatch).
